notes:
Demoted to medium not because the page is unclear -- it is the clearest page in the batch -- but because both of its gates are unmodellable: the weapon must be EQUIPPED rather than held, and the Masamune branch requires it be level 90~99, which is a property of the item that nothing observable reports. All three bullets are one interaction with one ???, so they collapse to a single step. Bullet 1 clicks it, bullet 2 is a dialogue menu (its sub-bullet only says that picking a type other than what you have equipped needs that weapon instead), bullet 3 hands the weapon over. None of the three is observable and a ??? can never carry a marker, so three rungs would be pure noise where one is honest.

This quest therefore has NO markable step. start is kept as Kupofried because the header names him and 'kupofried' folds to a usable NPC key; the alternative -- writing start as '???' -- resolves to an object with no key, which is fatal and would drop the quest entirely. If Kupofried is only the cutscene moogle and not a standing entity, the marker simply never appears, which is no worse than today.

The requirement is an EQUIPPED weapon, and equipment is not what the items check sees; recorded as items anyway with the caveat noted, since holding is the closest observable. Torigashira OR a level 90~99 Masamune is a real either/or, so the Masamune is items_alt. 'Level: 90~99' is a floor of 90 with a ceiling that is just the weapons' own level band and gates nothing extra. 'Quest Reqs: Guardian of the Void' names a quest while 'Previous' is empty, so it is recorded as the prerequisite it plainly is.

steps.note: one ???, three bullets: click it with the weapon equipped, choose Great Katana from the menu, then trade the weapon for the Tachi: Fudo unlock. The Masamune must be level 90~99. The page gives no grid for the ???.

notes:
Six bullets, four steps. Bullet 2 ('you will notice that only levels 7+ of the following jobs can equip the shield') is the header's 'Quest Reqs: Lv. 7 WAR / RDM / PLD / BST / SAM' restated in prose -- it is the gate, not an action, and a verb-scanner would have made a step of 'notice'. That gate is BOTH kinds at once, so level 7 AND five jobs; unlike 'a job at level 30+' this really does name specific jobs, and getting it wrong either way is expensive.

Bullet 4 ('equip the shield') is a precondition on the Bartolomeo meeting, not a rung of its own, so it merges there -- the whole point is that Bartolomeo recognises you by the shield. Equipment is not distinguishable from inventory by the items check, so the shield is recorded as items with the caveat noted.

Bullet 1 is a real step: you cannot start without the shield. It spans four zones (Auction House, or Young Quadavs in North Gustaberg, South Gustaberg, Palborough Mines, Konschtat Highlands), so it keeps no zone -- one step, one zone -- and the Young Quadav is carried as a drop so the glyph is right wherever you farm.

A textbook three-rung courier quest, and both key items are observable, so the ladder tracks it exactly. The unnumbered line above bullet 1 ('if you just completed Overnight Delivery, zone before continuing') is a precondition, not a step.

Two naming traps here, both checked against the resolver. Windurst Waters (South) is half of zone 238 and not a zone of its own, so the start zone is plain 'Windurst Waters'. And bullet 3 calls the filled canteen a 'Giddeus Water Canteen', which resolves to nothing -- the actual item is the 'Canteen of Giddeus water' the header's Item Reqs names, so that is what is recorded. The empty canteen resolves under both its long and abbreviated forms; the long one is used.

Bullet 2 offers the spring at (K-12) or (E-12). Both are the same named object in the same zone, so one step is enough and the second grid stays in the note -- a second rung would double-count one action, and a group would draw two markers for a choice the player only has to make once.

Medium because the walkthrough stops naming zones after bullet 1 and I had to carry Western Adoulin down to bullets 2 and 3 from the page's category and its own geography, rather than read it. If Kongramm's warehouse is not in Western Adoulin, step 2 has the wrong zone. Five bullets, four steps. Bullet 3 ('use the Rala Waterways entrance at F-5') is the route into bullet 4's ???, not an action of its own -- the entrance is in Western Adoulin and the ??? is in Rala Waterways, so a travel rung here would either take the wrong zone or point a zone marker at the far side of the door you are trying to find. The Misdelivered parcel is a key item, not an item -- it resolves as ki and not at all as item -- and it is granted at bullet 1, so it is step 1's evidence. Notably the page NEVER says where the parcel is handed over: not to Kongramm, not at the ???, not to Vaulois. Rather than guess, no later step requires holding it; if the ??? consumes it the ladder simply falls back on its own progress instead of stalling on a requirement the page never states.

The walkthrough drops the zone after bullet 1, but every location it names -- the Waterfront warehouse at (I-5), the Rala Waterways entrance at (F-5) -- is in Western Adoulin, and the page's only zone category is Western Adoulin, so that is carried down. notes:
The ladder is right but both gates are unmodellable -- being ON a CoP mission is not a predicate the schema has, and the 100 gil the Tonberry asks for cannot be expressed as an item -- so this sits at medium. Four bullets, three steps. Bullets 3 and 4 are two trades in a row to the SAME Tonberry -- the siredon, then the 100 gil he asks for -- with nothing observable between them, so they are one rung rather than two on one marker. Gil has no expressible form in the items schema, so the second half stays in the note; a gil count is the one requirement here the addon cannot check.

The walkthrough never says where Lourdaude stands, but the header's description does: 'the Tonberry that stands beside Anguenet', who is at (J-10). That is the page's own text, so the grid is carried rather than invented, and it is written down as a derivation in the note.

Bullet 2's sub-bullet says outright that you can buy the Muddy Siredon at the Auction House instead of fishing it, so Phanauet Channel is where the page points rather than a requirement -- the step is targetless anyway. The Blackened Siredon is the header's Reward and so is not evidence for the final trade.

'Quest Reqs: On the Chains of Promathia Mission Head Wind' is a MISSION state, not a completed quest, and the schema has only prev for it. Recorded there by title, as batch 4 did for Zilart Mission 13, and flagged: being 'on' a mission is not the same predicate as having finished a quest, and nothing observable distinguishes it.
